notes: The clerical error. A comedy, and the only tape in the shelf whose
**The comedy is entirely the examiner's.** Kim answers every question
patiently and correctly; what deteriorates is the professionalism of
the lieutenant obliged to ask them. Write the discomfort, never the
admiral's -- he has no discomfort, which is the point of him.
Two beats carry it and both are his, delivered flat. "Then I will
answer it as an ensign would. I remember." and "Seven years. Ask the
next one." The second is the whole of his career in six words and the
tape does not comment on it.
The ending is the examiner asking the human question off the sheet and
getting nothing. Forty seconds of silence on a tape is free and it is
the only thing in here that is not funny.
The arithmetic: Kim is born about 2349, returns from the Delta
Quadrant in 2378 at about twenty-nine, and is promoted flag rank in
2400 at about fifty-one. That makes this thirty-five years old when
Shepard dubs it, which is what the first dub line says.
title: Board of Examiners: oral re-examination
subtitle: Starfleet Personnel, first-year cadet syllabus
author: board recording; candidate's rank withheld on the slate
extra: Thirty-five years old. Filed under corrections.

lines.text: STARFLEET PERSONNEL: BOARD OF EXAMINERS
ORAL RE-EXAMINATION. FIRST-YEAR CADET SYLLABUS.
Thirty-five years old, and it should not exist at all.
A clerical error. The paperwork to fix it was worse.
Two people at a table. Nobody turns the recorder off.
For the record. State your name and rank, please.
Harry Kim. Admiral.
...Admiral.
That is the difficulty, yes.
The board has you down as an unverified first-year.
The board is correct. That is why I am here.
I am obliged to ask the questions as they are written.
I would be disappointed if you did not.
SECTION ONE: ASTROGATION
Define a subspace gradient. In your own words.
He defines it. It takes eleven seconds and is correct.
...Thank you. Second question. Warp field geometry.
He answers that one in nine seconds.
Do you want to sit the practical, or shall I mark it?
Ask me the questions. All of them. It is the rule.
SECTION TWO: PROTOCOL
You are an ensign. Your captain gives an unlawful order.
A pause. Not his. The examiner hears what he just said.
I withdraw nothing. The question is as it is written.
Then I will answer it as an ensign would. I remember.
...You were an ensign a long time, sir.
Seven years. Ask the next one.
SECTION THREE: EMERGENCY MEDICINE
Field dressing. Penetrating wound, no medical kit.
He describes it without stopping. He has done this.
That is better than the syllabus answer, sir.
Mark the syllabus answer. I do not want a note on it.
SECTION FOUR: ETHICS
Admiral, may I say something that is not on the sheet.
You may not. You will have to write it in the margin.
He writes something in the margin. It is not read out.
BOARD FINDING
Candidate passes. Credential verified. Rank confirmed.
Duration of clerical suspension: three months.
Three months. Nobody noticed until the promotion.
For the record, Admiral, this was absurd.
For the record, Lieutenant, it was the rules.
He shakes the examiner's hand. The recorder runs on.
...Sir. What did you actually do out there?
Forty seconds of nothing. Then a chair, and a door.
He never answers. I watch it for that part.
